headline.text: EU countries must apply the pay transparency rules by 7 June 2026, with pay gap reports for employers from 100 workers.

what_changed.text: Job applicants get the right to the starting pay or its range, and employers may not ask about pay history.
Employers with 150 to 249 workers must report their gender pay gap by 7 June 2027, then every three years.

who.text: All FR and ES employers, hospitality, retail and construction included, are covered through national law; pay gap reporting hits firms of 100 to 249 workers.

money.text: The text sets no fine amount; Member States set fines in national law, and worker compensation has no upper limit.

facts.statement: The directive covers employers in both the public and the private sector.

citation.quote: This Directive applies to employers in public and private sectors.

facts.statement: EU countries must bring the pay transparency rules into national law by 7 June 2026.

citation.quote: Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 7 June 2026.

facts.statement: Job applicants get the right to the starting pay or its range from the prospective employer.

citation.quote: the initial pay or its range, based on objective, gender-neutral criteria, to be attributed for the position concerned

facts.statement: Employers can give the pay information in a published job ad, before the job interview, or otherwise.

citation.quote: Such information shall be provided in a manner such as to ensure an informed and transparent negotiation on pay, such as in a published job vacancy notice, prior to the job interview or otherwise.

facts.statement: Employers may not ask applicants about their pay in current or previous jobs.

citation.quote: An employer shall not ask applicants about their pay history during their current or previous employment relationships.

facts.statement: Employers must give workers easy access to the criteria that set pay, pay levels and pay progression.

citation.quote: Employers shall make easily accessible to their workers the criteria that are used to determine workers’ pay, pay levels and pay progression.

facts.statement: EU countries may exempt employers with fewer than 50 workers from the pay progression duty.

citation.quote: Member States may exempt employers with fewer than 50 workers from the obligation related to the pay progression set out in paragraph 1.

facts.statement: Employers must tell all workers every year of their right to pay information and how to use it.

citation.quote: Employers shall inform all workers, on an annual basis, of their right to receive the information referred to in paragraph 1 and of the steps that the worker is to undertake to exercise that right.

facts.statement: Employers must answer a worker's request for pay levels by sex within two months.

citation.quote: Employers shall provide the information referred to in paragraph 1 within a reasonable period of time but in any event within two months from the date on which the request is made.

facts.statement: Employers with 250 workers or more must report pay gap data by 7 June 2027, then every year.

citation.quote: Employers with 250 workers or more shall, by 7 June 2027 and every year thereafter, provide the information set out in paragraph 1 relating to the previous calendar year.

facts.statement: Employers with 150 to 249 workers must report pay gap data by 7 June 2027, then every three years.

citation.quote: Employers with 150 to 249 workers shall, by 7 June 2027 and every three years thereafter, provide the information set out in paragraph 1 relating to the previous calendar year.

facts.statement: Employers with 100 to 149 workers must report pay gap data by 7 June 2031, then every three years.

citation.quote: Employers with 100 to 149 workers shall, by 7 June 2031 and every three years thereafter, provide the information set out in paragraph 1 relating to the previous calendar year.

facts.statement: EU countries may require pay reporting from employers with fewer than 100 workers.

citation.quote: Member States may, as a matter of national law, require employers with fewer than 100 workers to provide information on pay.

facts.statement: Reporting employers face a joint pay assessment when their report shows a gap of at least 5 % in any worker category.

citation.quote: the pay reporting demonstrates a difference in the average pay level between female and male workers of at least 5 % in any category of workers

facts.statement: EU countries must give employers with fewer than 250 workers technical assistance and training.

citation.quote: Member States shall provide support, in the form of technical assistance and training, to employers with fewer than 250 workers

facts.statement: EU countries must set fines under national law; the text sets no fine amount.

citation.quote: Those penalties shall include fines, the setting of which shall be based on national law.

facts.statement: Compensation for workers who suffer pay discrimination has no upper limit.

citation.quote: The compensation or reparation shall not be restricted by the fixing of a prior upper limit.

confidence.reason: The official text states every date, threshold and obligation used here, but French and Spanish transposing laws can add stricter rules.
